text.p: Agricultural equipment maker New Holland said on Thursday that its annual general meeting in Amsterdam had approved the payment of a regular dividend for 1996 of $0.55 per share.
In a statement, New Holland said the dividend is payable on June 16 1997 to shareholders of record on June 6 1997.

In November 1996, New Holland was partially spun off from Italy's industrial giant Fiat with its shares quoted on the New York Stock Exchange, while some 69 percent of the group is still retained by Fiat.

Last month, New Holland, which is the world's second largest maker of agricultural equipment after U.S. group John Deere, said its first quarter 1997 consolidated sales rose seven percent to $1.491 billion compared to first quarter 1996 levels.

The group had reported earlier this year that 1996 net income in accordance with U.S. GAAP accounting was $250 million after $221 million in 1995, while 1996 revenues rose to $5.547 billion from $5.0 billion in 1995.
